operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10010 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order created a board of three members to investigate the disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and other carriers named in List A and employees represented by the sixteen cooperating railway labor organizations named in List B; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in an organization of railway employees or in a carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 17, 1948); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred the carriers involved and their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the board's own report (a text of PDF pages 1-8 of 70 from the National Mediation Board site, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) carries the date December 17, 1948 on its title page and states that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report to the President until December 17; thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end. Executive Order 10015, signed November 5, 1948 and published at 13 FR 6601 in the Federal Register of November 9, 1948, amended this order effective as of October 18, 1948, the date its own text states: it adds six named carriers to List A and gives new designations to two organizations named in List B, so that after the amendment List A includes those six carriers and the two organizations carry the new designations. It does not change the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report requirement or the standstill, and it does not revoke or supersede this order; it is therefore a later amendment and not an end, and it is recorded as a later event on this clause. The same table in Executive Order 12553 also lists number 10015 with the subject "Amending an order creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", so the amending order was revoked on the same date by the same sentence.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10010
Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­
tigate D isputes  B etween  the A kron 
&  Barberton B elt R ailroad C ompany 
and O ther C arriers, and C ertain of 
Their  E mployees
WHEREAS disputes exist between the 
Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad Com­
pany and certain other carriers desig­
nated in List A attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the sixteen co­
operating railway labor organizations 
designated in List B attached hereto and 
made a part hereof; and 
WHEREAS these disputes have not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions jof the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threaten substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said disputes.
No member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of railway employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
disputes within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said disputes arose.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10009
R evoking in  P art E xecutive O rders N o. 
589 of M arch 14,1907, and N o. 1712 of 
F ebruary 24, 1913
WHEREAS Executive Order No. 589 of 
March 14,1907, recited in part that pass­
ports issued by the Government of Ja­
pan to Japanese or Korean citizens who 
were skilled or unskilled laborers to go 
to Mexico, Canada, or Hawaii 'were be­
ing used for the purpose of enabling the 
holders thereof to come to the conti­
nental territory of the United States to 
the detriment of labor conditions there­
in, and ordered that such citizens of Ja­
pan or Korea be refused permission to 
enter the continental territory of the 
United States and 
WHEREAS Executive Order No. 1712 
of February 24, 1913, recited that pass­
ports issued by certain foreign govern­
ments to their citizens or subjects, skilled 
or unskilled laborers, to go to countries 
or places other than the continental ter­
ritory of the United States were being 
used for the purpose of enabling the 
holders thereof to come to the x  conti­
nental territory of the United States to
the detriment of labor conditions there­
in, and ordered that such alien laborers, 
skilled or unskilled, be refused permis­
sion to enter the continental territory 
of the United States; and
WHEREAS the continued restraint 
imposed by the said Executive orders 
upon the freedom of Japanese or Korean 
citizens or subjects who entered the Ter­
ritory of Hawaii under the passports 
referred to above to come to the con­
tinental United States has resulted in 
considerable personal hardship to such 
persons; and
WHEREAS the number of Japanese 
or Korean citizens or subjects thus pro­
hibited from entering the continental 
United States from the Territory of Ha­
waii is so small, and the age of such 
persons is so advanced, that their entry 
into the continental United States would 
no longer be a detriment to labor con­
ditions therein:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 3 of the 
Immigration Act of 1917 (39 Stat. 875; 
8 U. S. C. 136), I hereby revoke the said 
Executive Orders No. 589 of March 14, 
1907, and No. 1712 of February 24, 1913, 
to the extent that they are applicable 
to Japanese or Korean citizens or sub­
jects who entered the Territory of Hawaii 
under the aforesaid passports and who 
are now precluded from legally enterr 
ing or remaining in the continental ter­
ritory of the United States by reason of 
such Executive orders.
The Commissioner of Immigration and 
Naturalization is hereby authorized and 
directed, with the approval of the At­
torney General, to take such action and 
to issue such rules and regulations as 
may be necessary for carrying out the 
provisions of this order.
H arry S. Truman
The W hite H ouse,
October 18, 1948.
[F. R. Doc. 48-9261, Filed Oct. 18, 1948;
11:50 a. m.]

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (13 FR 6104, the issue of October 19, 1948; the order begins on PDF page 6 and its attached lists continue on page 7) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10010, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company dispute, and is signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House on October 18, 1948. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Prior research: a filed claim for this order exists (research/readiness/claims/claude-2026-10-31-apollo-g03.jsonl, line 11) and carries an independent AI whole-case review, but its reasoning described Executive Order 10015 as an amendment without recording it as a later event with a source; this version records it from the Federal Register text of Executive Order 10015 and keeps the end date. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete with no coverage warning and no scope note. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order; the Federal Register catalog search found the two instruments recorded here (the amendment of November 5, 1948 and the revocation of February 25, 1986).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 17, 1948), and a standstill that runs from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the board's own report (a text of PDF pages 1-8 of 70 from the National Mediation Board site, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) carries the date December 17, 1948 on its title page and states that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report to the President until December 17; thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949. These dates are leads and are not recorded as later events, because no claim-grade source and no reviewed factual-event record for the report is held for this order; they are also not claimed as an end, and the clause is described only as functionally spent. The dossier chain, the Federal Register catalog disposition note for this order (amended by Executive Order 10015 of November 5, 1948; revoked by Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986) and my reading of the held texts of Executive Order 10015 and Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25. Executive Order 10015 is an amendment of the attached lists and is recorded as a later event, not as an end.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The recitals incorporate the lists by reference to identify the carriers and the railway labor organizations, and the lists contain no command; Executive Order 10015 later amended them. savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one railway labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
